acceptance.output_evidence: rc=0. TABLE VERBATIM: `=== OS-s-12 WORKING-ORDER CENSUS -- outset tools ===` / `plane: LOCAL REPO CLI (.tools/<tool> in this worktree) | probe deadline 9s | census budget 100s | elapsed 29.3s` / `tool               rc  verdict                     state  vintg  budget       secs` / `comp-heat           0  WORKING                     False  False  YES          0.7` / `comp-fedobs         0  WORKING                     False  True   not-accepted 6.4` / `comp-drift          0  WORKING                     False  False  NO-LINE      2.6` / `comp-xray           0  WORKING                     False  False  not-accepted 3.7` / `comp-similar        0  WORKING                     True   True   NO-LINE      2.4` / `comp-pipescript   124  FAILED                      False  False  not-accepted 9.8   [bounded at 9s, no answer]` / `comp-freshness      0  WORKING                     False  False  not-accepted 1.2` / `comp-blast          0  WORKING                     True   False  not-accepted 1.9` / `comp-estate         0  WORKING                     False  False  YES          0.6` / `DENOMINATOR: 9 tool(s) censused; 8 WORKING, 1 FAILED, 0 NO-ANSWER-DISCLOSED, 0 NOT-PROBED-BUDGET-EXHAUSTED` / `disclosure over the 9: answer-state 2/9, vintage 2/9, budget-line-when-offered 2/4`. COLUMN GRAINS, stated because a census's columns are where grain slips: `rc` is the exit code of a REAL answer probe, never --help (--help proves the CLI parses, not that the tool answers); `WORKING` requires rc=0 AND a non-trivial body; `NO-ANSWER-DISCLOSED` is the confident-zero shape (rc=0, empty body); `budget` is YES only when --budget was offered AND a disclosure line printed, `NO-LINE` when offered and silently swallowed (the NFRA_OUTSET-S6 shape), `not-accepted` when the tool exposes no --budget at all. THE PLANE COUNTED: the LOCAL REPO CLI plane (.tools/<tool> in this worktree at 22e38e7963) -- NOT the ~/bin shim plane, NOT any deployed plane, NOT the engines called as functions. THE ONE FAILED ROW, re-probed to separate slow from not-answering: `comp-pipescript deployed @75s bound: rc=124 elapsed=75.7s timed_out=True bytes=82`, the 82 bytes being only its shim line; kept in the table at FAILED rather than dropped, because the brief names it and 'could not answer within the bound' IS its working-order answer (filed as NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S9). NOT DIAGNOSED: why it does not answer -- the CLI's behaviour is measured, the cause is not, and no AWS plane was read.

mutant.description: Three planted/negative controls, because a census is the most exposed thing on this project to the false-zero family and an unrun falsifier is a promise. (i) ABSENT-TOOL PLANT: append a tool that does not exist and require it to read FAILED AND to remain in the denominator. (ii) CONFIDENT-ZERO PLANT: rc=0 with an empty body must not score WORKING. (iii) INSTRUMENT NEGATIVE CONTROL: dispatch a known-good bash launcher the naive way (bare 'bash') and require that it FALSELY fails while the resolver dispatch succeeds on the same tool -- proving the census's dispatch discriminates and that a non-zero is obtainable on a case known to exist.
mutant.expected: (i) planted row FAILED and denominator grows 2 -> 3; (ii) classify(rc=0, empty) is NO-ANSWER-DISCLOSED, never WORKING; (iii) bare-bash rc!=0 on a tool the resolver runs at rc=0.
mutant.observed: ALL THREE FIRED. (i) `A4 planted failure reads FAILED and is counted in the denominator -- denominator 3 (subset was 2); planted verdict=FAILED`. (ii) `A5 rc=0 with an empty body is not scored WORKING -- classify(rc=0, empty) -> NO-ANSWER-DISCLOSED`. (iii) `A6 positive control: resolver dispatch answers where bare-bash falsely fails -- resolver rc=0 bytes=973; bare-bash rc=1 bytes=504 wsl_stub=True`. A FOURTH CONTROL FIRED DURING CONSTRUCTION AND CHANGED THE BUILD: the first discovery pass dispatched bare 'bash' and returned rc=1 for ALL FOUR bash-launcher tools with body length EXACTLY 504 bytes each. Four independent failures do not share a byte length; one shared dependency failing does. That tell (CLAUDE.md s.2 -- a check scoped to the members cannot see a defect in what the members share) is what exposed the WSL-stub trap, which would have marked 4 of 9 outset tools BROKEN with a clean denominator and every verdict false. Filed as NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S7 with a live victim measured at .tools/drift_producer.py:155. A FIFTH: subprocess timeout= failed to bound comp-pipescript (91.8 s against an 8 s deadline) because the launcher's grandchild holds the pipe; fixed with file-redirect plus process-tree kill (8.9 s) and pinned as arm A7, filed as NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S8.

determinism.method: The battery was run twice end to end under `timeout 120` and the two outputs compared on every verdict-bearing field -- per-tool verdicts, the DENOMINATOR line, the disclosure counts and the final PASS line -- with wall-clock seconds normalised out, since elapsed time is not a verdict-bearing column.
determinism.observed: Run 1 rc=0 and run 2 rc=0; the compared fields were IDENTICAL across both runs (`DETERMINISM: verdicts/denominators IDENTICAL across two runs`), including `8 WORKING, 1 FAILED` and `answer-state 2/9, vintage 2/9, budget-line-when-offered 2/4`. Only `secs` varied. DECLARED DEPENDENCE, not hidden: comp-fedobs reads a served artifact, so its row depends on that artifact's reachability at run time, and comp-pipescript's FAILED verdict depends on it continuing not to answer within the probe deadline -- both are properties of the world the census exists to report, not instability in the census.

declared_exclusions.reason: The sweep behind NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S7 is a narrow lexical pattern (`["bash"` in tracked *.py, 17 hits, 1 live production call site); a call built from a variable, via shell=True, or spelled '/bin/bash' would not match. Stated as a limit on that row and left to its named disarm owner rather than silently presented as complete.

This order declares depends_on OS-s-1 and OS-s-4; OS-s-1 is landed and OS-s-4 is not. OS-s-4 adds vintage and catalog disclosure to `comp-heat federated`, so comp-heat's vintage column here is a PRE-OS-s-4 reading and is expected to change. No arm depends on OS-s-4's output, so this is a stated vintage bound rather than a blocker; the census is the instrument and re-running it is the re-measurement.

surprises: NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S7: ARMED -- on this host a bare `subprocess.run(["bash", <script>])` resolves to the System32 WSL stub (no distribution) and returns rc=1 with a UTF-16LE error body, so a census dispatching that way marks 4 of the 9 outset tools BROKEN with a clean denominator and every verdict FALSE; caught because all four bodies were exactly 504 bytes, and measured live at .tools/drift_producer.py:155 which makes that call and counts rc!=0 as tools_failed. Remedy is the estate's own .tools/git_bash_resolver.py; filed not fixed (outside <paths>), disarm owner named.

NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S8: subprocess timeout= does not bound a shell-launcher comp-tool, because the launcher's python grandchild holds the inherited stdout pipe -- `comp-pipescript deployed` ran 91.8 s under an 8 s deadline and the aggregate pass then died at an outer bound with zero output, the same shape as NFRA_OUTSET-S2. File-redirect plus process-tree kill returns the same probe at 8.9 s; pinned as standing arm A7.

NFRA_OUTSET-W3-S9: census result -- `comp-pipescript deployed`, the brief's own named GIT->DEPLOY-hop tool, returned no answer at a 9 s bound and none at a 75 s re-probe (82 bytes, its shim line only), and accepts no --budget for a caller to bound it with. 8 of 9 outset tools answer; this is the one that does not. Reported in the table at FAILED rather than omitted, per brief O5.
